Markus / Laura,

Thanks for the walkthrough this morning. Attached is our latest MAP (Stella_MAP_v3.xlsx) — I populated the acceptance criteria column with what Legal and Procurement asked for. We are good on the evaluation plan (test harness + 2-week pilot) but Procurement is pushing for final contract signatures to align with Q1 budgets.

Two things I want to surface:
- Procurement flagged a required SOC 2 report and a short window for on-site security review (they want materials by next Wednesday).
- Our C-level wants firm close by 2026-02-01. If we miss that, their internal incentive pools shift and the deal gets reprioritized.

Can Redwood commit to the security packet delivery and a staged acceptance approach if Procurement takes longer than expected? If not, we need to re-baseline dates now.

Attachments: Stella_MAP_v3.xlsx (MAP), evaluation-checklist.docx (referenced)

Jorge —

Appreciate the clarity. Short answer: yes, we can support a staged acceptance and will prioritize the security artifact bundle. Proposed immediate steps:

1) We push an initial security packet (SOC2 summary, data flow diagram, access control overview) by EOD Tuesday (2026-01-14).
2) Agree to a 2-week pilot window starting 2026-01-20 with a soft-accept milestone at +7 days and final acceptance at +14 days.
3) If Procurement needs additional review beyond next Wednesday, we will accept staged signoff: Pilot OK -> limited production access -> full production after procurement finish.

I'm attaching a short bridging proposal that maps the MAP milestones to the staged acceptance flow (redwood-bridging-proposal.pdf).

Laura / Neha — can you take point on the SOC2 summary + designate the engineer for the data-flow schematic? I will loop Sales Ops if we need to reserve burst capacity for pilot traffic.

Markus
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood-bridging-proposal.pdf

Thanks Markus — that plan is workable. A couple of clarifications:
- Procurement still needs the SOC2 scan logs (not full report) and a named Redwood contact for the on-site review.
- For staged acceptance, the C-suite asked that any production enablement requires an executive signoff email (so they have an approval trail).

Marie (cc) will consolidate Procurement's exact artifact list. If Redwood can provide the SOC2 summary + logs sample by Tuesday and a single point of contact for the on-site review, we can hold to the 02/01 close as long as the pilot shows no material regressions.

Jorge

Team — internal note (will keep Jorge looped):

I reviewed Procurement's artifact list and matched it to our standard pack. Two risk items to record in our internal MAP risk log:
1) Procurement timeline variance — medium risk. Likelihood: probable if legal redlines hit. Impact: slip of close >2 weeks. Mitigation: staged acceptance + executive email signoff (Markus to confirm).
2) Pilot traffic spike — low-medium risk. Likelihood: possible if Stella exercises burst capacity. Impact: cost & potential SLO pressure. Mitigation: reserve 48h burst capacity and activate auto-throttle.

Action items assigned: Neha to prepare SOC2 summary + sample logs by 2026-01-14 17:00 PST (deliverable: SOC2_packet.zip). Rishi to draft the executive signoff email template and procurement fallback clause. I attached the risk export for the deal (risk_log_20260113.csv).

I'll escalate to Sales Leadership if Procurement requests contract language that materially increases credit/exposure.

Laura Bennett
